title: Psalms Chapter 85 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 85 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 85 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 85.

questions.question: Who is the Psalm for in Psalms 85?
questions.explanation: The Psalm is described as being for the sons of Korah in the title of the chapter (Psalms 85:1).

questions.question: What has the LORD brought back according to Psalms 85?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the LORD has brought back the captivity of Jacob (Psalms 85:1).

questions.question: True or False: The LORD has forgiven the iniquity of His people.
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that the LORD has forgiven the iniquity of His people (Psalms 85:2).

questions.question: What has the LORD covered according to Psalms 85:2?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the LORD has covered all their sin (Psalms 85:2).

questions.question: What does the Psalmist ask God to turn away from in Psalms 85:4?
questions.explanation: The verse asks God to cause His anger toward them to cease (Psalms 85:4).

questions.question: True or False: The Psalmist believes the LORD will be angry with them forever.
questions.explanation: The Psalmist questions whether the LORD will be angry forever (Psalms 85:5), implying he does not believe it will be the case.

questions.question: What does the Psalmist desire in Psalms 85:6?
options: To be restored to the land
questions.explanation: The verse expresses a desire for revival so that God's people may rejoice (Psalms 85:6).

questions.question: What does the Psalmist ask God to show in Psalms 85:7?
questions.explanation: The verse specifically asks for God's mercy and salvation (Psalms 85:7).

questions.question: True or False: The Psalmist will hear what God the LORD will speak.
questions.explanation: The Psalmist declares that he will hear what God the LORD will speak (Psalms 85:8).

questions.question: What does the Lord speak to His people according to Psalms 85:8?
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that God will speak peace unto His people (Psalms 85:8).

questions.question: In Psalms 85, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
questions.explanation: The first instruction given in the Psalm is to turn us, O God (Psalms 85:4).

questions.question: What two attributes are said to have met together in Psalms 85:10?
questions.explanation: The verse states that mercy and truth have met together (Psalms 85:10).

questions.question: True or False: Righteousness shall spring out of the earth according to Psalms 85.
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that truth shall spring out of the earth (Psalms 85:11).

questions.question: What will the LORD give according to Psalms 85:12?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the LORD shall give that which is good (Psalms 85:12).

questions.question: What shall go before the LORD according to Psalms 85:13?
questions.explanation: The verse states that righteousness shall go before Him (Psalms 85:13).

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 85 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 85 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 85:6, what is the desired outcome when God revives His people?
options: That His people may rejoice in Him
That His people may receive wealth
That His people may conquer their enemies
That His people may build temples
questions.correctAnswer: That His people may rejoice in Him
questions.explanation: Psalms 85:6 specifically states that revival by God is so that 'thy people may rejoice in thee.' This highlights the joy and renewed relationship with God as the key outcome.

questions.question: What two requests does the psalmist make in Psalms 85:7?
questions.explanation: Psalms 85:7 petitions God to 'Shew us thy mercy, O LORD, and grant us thy salvation,' focusing on God's compassionate forgiveness and deliverance.

questions.question: According to Psalms 85:8, what will God speak to His people and saints?
questions.explanation: Psalms 85:8 says God 'will speak peace unto his people, and to his saints,' emphasizing the message of peace from God to those who follow Him.

questions.question: How does Psalms 85:8 warn believers about their response to God's message?
options: Not to turn again to folly
questions.correctAnswer: Not to turn again to folly
questions.explanation: The verse instructs believers to heed God’s message and cautions them 'but let them not turn again to folly,' warning against foolishness after receiving God's peace.

questions.question: What does Psalms 85:9 say is near to those who fear God?
questions.explanation: Psalms 85:9 declares, 'Surely his salvation is nigh them that fear him,' showing that salvation is close to those who reverence God.

questions.question: What is the result in the land when salvation is near, according to Psalms 85:9?
options: That glory may dwell in our land
questions.correctAnswer: That glory may dwell in our land
questions.explanation: The verse links salvation being near with 'that glory may dwell in our land,' implying divine favor and honor resting on the land.

questions.question: What relationship between mercy and truth is described in Psalms 85:10?
questions.explanation: Psalms 85:10 poetically states 'Mercy and truth are met together,' illustrating harmony between God's compassion and faithfulness.

questions.question: According to Psalms 85:10, what action symbolizes the union of righteousness and peace?
questions.explanation: The verse metaphorically describes 'righteousness and peace have kissed each other,' symbolizing perfect unity between moral rightness and harmony.

questions.question: What does Psalms 85:11 say about the origins of truth and righteousness?
options: Truth springs out of the earth; righteousness looks down from heaven
Truth comes from heaven; righteousness from the earth
Both truth and righteousness come from heaven
Both truth and righteousness come from the earth
questions.correctAnswer: Truth springs out of the earth; righteousness looks down from heaven
questions.explanation: The verse contrasts the sources: 'Truth shall spring out of the earth; and righteousness shall look down from heaven,' showing a divine and earthly cooperation.

questions.question: What promise does Psalms 85:12 give about the land?
options: Our land shall yield her increase
Our land shall be taken away
questions.correctAnswer: Our land shall yield her increase
questions.explanation: Psalms 85:12 promises that 'our land shall yield her increase,' indicating blessing and productivity as a result of God's goodness.

questions.question: According to Psalms 85:12, who gives that which is good?
questions.explanation: The verse affirms that 'the LORD shall give that which is good,' emphasizing God's role as the provider of blessings.

questions.question: Based on Psalms 85:13, what role does righteousness play in relation to God?
options: It goes before Him and sets us in His way
questions.correctAnswer: It goes before Him and sets us in His way
questions.explanation: Psalms 85:13 states, 'Righteousness shall go before him; and shall set us in the way of his steps,' showing righteousness as a guide to following God.

questions.question: What does Psalms 85:7 imply about the relationship between mercy and salvation?
questions.explanation: The verse links the request for mercy with the granting of salvation, implying mercy is foundational to receiving salvation from God.

questions.question: What does Psalms 85:9 promise will happen if the people fear God as instructed in Psalms 85:8?
options: Salvation will be near them and glory will dwell in the land
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation will be near them and glory will dwell in the land
questions.explanation: Psalms 85:8 commands believers not to turn to folly, and Psalms 85:9 promises salvation and glory to those who fear God, connecting obedience to blessing.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 85:8 emphasizes listening to God because He will speak peace only to the wicked.
questions.explanation: Psalms 85:8 says God will speak peace unto 'his people, and to his saints,' not to the wicked, so the statement is false.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 85 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 85.

questions.question: According to Psalms 85:11, what are the two elements described as springing or looking down?
questions.explanation: Psalms 85:11 states, 'Truth shall spring out of the earth; and righteousness shall look down from heaven,' clearly identifying these two elements.

questions.question: In Psalms 85:12, what does the LORD promise to give that will cause the land to yield its increase?
questions.explanation: The verse says, 'Yea, the LORD shall give that which is good; and our land shall yield her increase,' indicating that the LORD's giving of 'good' results in the land's productivity.

questions.question: What role does righteousness play according to Psalms 85:13?
options: It goes before God and sets us in His steps
It is a punishment for sin
questions.correctAnswer: It goes before God and sets us in His steps
questions.explanation: Psalms 85:13 says, 'Righteousness shall go before him; and shall set us in the way of his steps,' indicating righteousness leads and guides us.

questions.question: Which other biblical passage echoes the theme of 'mercy and truth meeting together' as in Psalms 85:10?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 3:3 states, 'Let not mercy and truth forsake thee,' reflecting the same theme of mercy and truth meeting as in Psalms 85:10.

questions.question: What literary device is primarily used in Psalms 85:10 where 'Mercy and truth are met together; righteousness and peace have kissed each other'?
questions.explanation: The verse personifies abstract concepts (mercy, truth, righteousness, peace) as meeting and kissing each other, which is personification.

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated as 'truth' in Psalms 85:10 and 11 is 'emet.' What is the broader theological significance of this term in Hebrew scripture?
options: It denotes faithfulness and reliability of God
questions.correctAnswer: It denotes faithfulness and reliability of God
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'emet' (truth) encompasses faithfulness, reliability, and covenantal steadfastness of God, themes central in Psalms 85:10-11.

questions.question: Psalms 85:9 says salvation is near to those who fear God. Which New Testament verse echoes this concept of fear and salvation?
questions.explanation: Acts 10:34-35 says God shows no partiality but accepts those who fear Him and do what is right, echoing the connection of fear of God and salvation in Psalms 85:9.

questions.question: How does Psalms 85:12's promise of the land yielding increase relate to the covenant blessings in Deuteronomy 28?
options: It reflects the blessing of agricultural prosperity for obedience
It contradicts the curses described in Deuteronomy
It predicts the exile of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects the blessing of agricultural prosperity for obedience
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 28 promises that obedience to God will bring blessing including fertile land and abundance, paralleling Psalms 85:12's promise of the land yielding increase.

questions.question: Which Old Testament book also uses the imagery of righteousness leading or going before God, similar to Psalms 85:13?
questions.explanation: Isaiah repeatedly uses the theme of righteousness preparing the way for God’s coming (e.g., Isaiah 40:3), paralleling Psalms 85:13.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 85:8 encourages the people to turn back to folly after hearing God speak peace.
questions.explanation: Psalms 85:8 says, 'but let them not turn again to folly,' instructing the people not to return to foolishness after hearing God's peace.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 85:5 expresses concern that God might be angry forever and across all generations.
questions.explanation: The verse asks, 'Wilt thou be angry with us for ever? wilt thou draw out thine anger to all generations?' showing concern about prolonged divine anger.

questions.question: What does Psalms 85:7 request from the LORD?
questions.explanation: Psalms 85:7 says, 'Shew us thy mercy, O LORD, and grant us thy salvation,' directly requesting mercy and salvation.

questions.question: How does the chapter's focus on restoration and peace in Psalms 85 relate to the historical context of post-exilic Israel?
options: It reflects hopes for national restoration after Babylonian exile
It predicts the destruction of Jerusalem
It focuses on the wilderness wanderings
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects hopes for national restoration after Babylonian exile
questions.explanation: The psalm’s themes of forgiveness, revival, and peace align with the post-exilic period when Israel sought restoration after captivity, as referenced in Psalms 85:1.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage uses the concept of 'peace' spoken by God to His people similar to Psalms 85:8?
questions.explanation: John 14:27 quotes Jesus saying, 'Peace I leave with you,' echoing the theme of God speaking peace to His people as in Psalms 85:8.

questions.question: Which verse in Psalms 85 expresses the plea for God to 'turn us' and cease His anger?
questions.explanation: Psalms 85:4 states, 'Turn us, O God of our salvation, and cause thine anger toward us to cease,' clearly expressing this plea.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 85 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 85 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine action is described in Psalms 85:1 that demonstrates God's mercy toward His people?
options: Bringing back the captivity of Jacob
questions.correctAnswer: Bringing back the captivity of Jacob
questions.explanation: Psalms 85:1 states that the LORD has been favourable to the land and brought back the captivity of Jacob, demonstrating His mercy by restoring His people from exile.

questions.question: According to Psalms 85:2, what has God done with the sins of His people?
options: Forgiven and covered all their sin
questions.correctAnswer: Forgiven and covered all their sin
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly states that God has forgiven the iniquity of His people and covered all their sin, highlighting divine forgiveness and grace.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is most clearly revealed in Psalms 85:3 where His wrath is taken away?
questions.explanation: Psalms 85:3 speaks of God taking away His wrath and turning from anger, which reveals the attribute of mercy as God withholds deserved punishment.

questions.question: What petition is made in Psalms 85:4 that reflects a desire for restoration and peace?
options: Turn us, O God of our salvation, and cause thine anger toward us to cease
Send us a mighty warrior to fight our battles
Remove all enemies from our land
questions.correctAnswer: Turn us, O God of our salvation, and cause thine anger toward us to cease
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly petitions God to turn His anger away and restore His people, indicating a deep longing for reconciliation and peace.

questions.question: What theological concern is expressed in Psalms 85:5 regarding the duration of God's anger?
options: Will God be angry forever and extend His wrath to all generations?
Will God forget His covenant forever?
Will God abandon the temple forever?
Will God punish only the current generation?
questions.correctAnswer: Will God be angry forever and extend His wrath to all generations?
questions.explanation: The verse questions whether God's anger will last forever and be drawn out to all generations, reflecting the theological tension between divine justice and mercy.

questions.question: What hope for revival and rejoicing is articulated in Psalms 85:6?
options: Wilt thou not revive us again: that thy people may rejoice in thee?
Will you send a messenger to lead us?
Shall we build a new temple?
Will we conquer our enemies by might?
questions.correctAnswer: Wilt thou not revive us again: that thy people may rejoice in thee?
questions.explanation: This verse expresses a hope that God will revive His people so that they may rejoice in Him, emphasizing spiritual renewal and joy in salvation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Psalms 85:7 when the psalmist asks to see 'thy mercy' and receive 'thy salvation'?
questions.explanation: The request to show mercy and grant salvation reveals God's attribute of mercy, His compassion toward sinners and willingness to save.

questions.question: According to Psalms 85:8, what does God promise to speak to His people?
questions.explanation: Verse 8 declares that God will speak peace unto His people and saints, indicating divine communication bringing tranquility and restoration.

questions.question: What combined theological truth is taught by Psalms 85:10 and Psalms 85:11 regarding the relationship between mercy, truth, righteousness, and peace?
options: Mercy and truth meet, righteousness and peace kiss, with truth springing from earth and righteousness looking from heaven
Mercy and wrath coexist, righteousness punishes, peace is absent
Truth is hidden, mercy is withdrawn, peace is delayed
Righteousness is earthly only, mercy is conditional
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy and truth meet, righteousness and peace kiss, with truth springing from earth and righteousness looking from heaven
questions.explanation: Psalms 85:10 speaks of mercy and truth meeting and righteousness and peace kissing, while 85:11 shows truth springing from earth and righteousness looking down from heaven, together illustrating the harmonious unity of divine attributes that bring salvation.

questions.question: How does Psalms 85:12 emphasize God's providential blessing on the land?
options: The LORD shall give that which is good; and our land shall yield her increase
The land shall be cursed for disobedience
Enemies shall invade and desolate the land
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD shall give that which is good; and our land shall yield her increase
questions.explanation: Verse 12 highlights God's providence by promising goodness and fruitful increase in the land, reflecting His care for creation and His covenant blessings.

questions.question: What does Psalms 85:13 teach about the role of righteousness in the divine plan?
options: Righteousness goes before God and sets us in His way
questions.correctAnswer: Righteousness goes before God and sets us in His way
questions.explanation: This verse shows that righteousness precedes God’s coming and directs His people in His steps, portraying righteousness as guiding and preparatory in God's redemptive work.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Psalms 85 shows a God who is inconsistent, alternating between wrath and mercy without clear purpose. What does Psalms 85:3-6 actually teach about God's wrath and mercy?
options: God takes away His wrath and turns from anger, but the people still seek revival and cessation of anger
God is wrathful and never shows mercy
God is merciful but ignores justice
God's anger is arbitrary and unending
questions.correctAnswer: God takes away His wrath and turns from anger, but the people still seek revival and cessation of anger
questions.explanation: Verses 3-6 reveal a God who removes wrath and turns from anger, yet His people petition for revival and peace, showing a consistent divine plan balancing justice and mercy. This refutes claims of inconsistency (Psalms 85:3-6).

questions.question: What doctrine about divine forgiveness and restoration is taught by combining Psalms 85:1-2 and Psalms 85:7?
options: God forgives the iniquity of His people and shows mercy, granting salvation
God withholds forgiveness and delays salvation
Forgiveness is conditional on human merit
Salvation must be earned through works
questions.correctAnswer: God forgives the iniquity of His people and shows mercy, granting salvation
questions.explanation: Verses 1-2 affirm God's forgiveness of sins, while verse 7 pleads for His mercy and salvation, together teaching the doctrine of divine forgiveness and mercy leading to salvation.

questions.question: What narrative arc connection to the broader redemptive story is seen in Psalms 85:9 where salvation is near to those who fear God so that glory may dwell in the land?
options: It anticipates the Messianic era of peace and God's reign on earth
It refers only to ancient Israel with no future hope
It predicts the destruction of the temple
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates the Messianic era of peace and God's reign on earth
questions.explanation: The nearness of salvation and the dwelling of glory in the land foreshadow the Messianic kingdom where God's presence and peace are fully realized, connecting to the grand narrative of redemption.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is most emphasized in Psalms 85:8, where God promises to speak peace to His people and saints?
questions.explanation: God’s promise to speak peace in verse 8 reveals His attribute as the giver of peace, emphasizing His role in reconciliation and restoration.
